3. Plaint case in short, inter alia, is that Sutu Bibi, mother of the defendants sold 0.84 acres of land appertaining to SA Khatian Nos. 163, 119, 106, 74 and 102 under mouza Dhadua Police Station Batiaghata, District Khulna to the plaintiff on 3-1-2006, at a consideration money of Taka 80,000 on condition that she will execute and register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff after release of her son from jail. She delivered the possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff. But ultimately she failed to register the sale deed inspite of legal notice of the plaintiff and died later on. The heirs of Sutu Bibi who are the defendant in the present suit, did not register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff. Plaintiff has been possession the suit land. On 1-10-09 defendant threatened to dispossess the plaintiff. Hence he filed the suit. 

 4. Defendant No. 1 and 3-4 contested the suit by filing separate written statement, denying the plaint case, stating, inter alia, that their mother never entered into an oral agreement of sale of the suit land with the plaintiff nor she had accepted any consideration money. She never transferred possession of the suit land to the plaintiff. Rather they as the legal heirs of Sutu Bibi are possessing the suit land. The DP Khatian No. 155 has correctly been prepared in the name of Sutu Bibi regarding the suit land. The defendant No.4 transferred 0.2769 acres of land to the defendant No.3 vide registered deed of heba-bil-ewaj No. 435 dated 18-1-2012. The question of threatening the plaintiff to dispossess is false and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 14. From going through the record, it is apparent that plaintiff no way has succeed to prove that he got 0.84 acres of land (that is a suit land from Sutu Bibi) and is in possession thereon. PWs 2 and 3 although said in their deposition that they have seen the plaintiff to possess the land but admittedly plaintiff is also a cosharer in the khatian and accordingly it cannot be said he is not in possession in the suit land. But in the absence of the evidence to prove that there was at all any oral agreement to transfer the suit land in favour of the plaintiff by his vendor, it is very difficult to assess that plaintiff by any means got delivery of possession through any oral agreement. When the plaintiff could not succeed to prove the alleged sale as well as delivery of possession in his favour of the suit land, the possession as been claim by the plaintiff in the land is nothing but his possession as a co-sharer in the suit premises.
